PART 8 — Toolkit, Case Index, FAQ and Sources

8.1 A One-Page Response Card

When exposed or woundedSay or do
Body (Move 1)Long exhale. Drop shoulders and jaw. No reply for an hour.
Name (Move 2)"I feel ___ because I need ___."
Sort (Move 3)True / partly true / false / contempt / unknown.
Verdict (Move 4)"The lie being pressed is: I am not ___."
Receive (Move 5)"I am held. I was loved before this and I am loved now."
Choose (Move 6)Silence / short truth / warmth / firmness / distance / process / repair.
Lament and entrust (Move 7)Say the rage to God. "I release this verdict into your hands."
Accompany (Move 8)Tell one safe person today.

8.2 Prayer Based on Ephesians 1:17-19

Father, give me — and give those I love who live as servants in your house — a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of you. Enlighten the eyes of our hearts, that we may know the hope to which you have called us, and what is the richness of the inheritance that is already ours. Where we are in a far country, bring us to ourselves. Where we are inside and cannot feast, meet us at the door. Amen.

8.4 FAQ

QuestionAnswer
Is it wrong to want the person who hurt me to face consequences?No. Wanting accountability, safety and truth is different from wanting them to suffer (Part 5.6's motive test). Pursue consequences through legitimate processes.
Is "living well is the best revenge" okay?Living well is good; making your life a rebuttal to them keeps them as your audience. Aim to live well because it is good, not because they are watching.
I feel nothing but hatred. Is that unforgivable?It is human. Name it to God and a safe person (Part 5.7); hatred often sits on top of grief and powerlessness. If it is consuming you, a counsellor can help.
Is there a difference between justice and justifying myself?Yes. Justice seeks right to be done; self-justification seeks my image to be preserved (Part 4). The test is whether I'm willing to be wrong.
Do I have to wait for an apology before moving on?No (Part 6.1, move 8). An apology would help, but it is theirs to give.
If God never leaves, why do I feel He's absent?Feeling and fact can diverge; Scripture records saints who felt abandoned (Ps 22; 88) while God was near. Lament is welcome; so is a safe friend and, where needed, professional help.
Does Part 7 mean everyone is saved?No. It distinguishes constancy of God's love and presence from the experience of reconciliation, and it flags that Christians disagree about the final scope of salvation.

8.5 Sources and Limits

Research cited. Carlsmith, Wilson & Gilbert (2008), "The paradoxical consequences of revenge," Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 95(6), 1316-1324 (a set of laboratory studies; findings are from a specific experimental setting). de Quervain et al. (2004), "The neural basis of altruistic punishment," Science, 305, 1254-1258. Strang, Sherman, Mayo-Wilson, Woods & Ariel (2013), restorative justice conferencing systematic review, Campbell Systematic Reviews 2013:12 (see also Sherman et al., 2015, Journal of Quantitative Criminology). U.S. National Institute of Justice, "Five Things About Deterrence" (2016; NCJ 247350). From general knowledge, not re-verified in this session: Festinger (1957) on cognitive dissonance; Tavris & Aronson, Mistakes Were Made (But Not by Me); Tangney & Dearing (2002) on shame and guilt; Zehr, Changing Lenses (1990); Freyd's description of DARVO. Word studies reflect standard lexicons and commonly agreed renderings; nuances vary among scholars. Theology. Claims about God's restoration, union and the awakening of ignorant believers are the relational-gospel framework of this series; Kruger's positions are represented only at the level of the framework summarised earlier, with no verbatim quotation. Christians disagree on retribution versus restoration, on divine initiative and human response, and on the final scope of salvation; those places are flagged. All named individuals in cases are composites. This is not legal, medical or counselling advice. If you are in danger, contact local emergency services (112 in India) or a trusted professional; if you are thinking of harming yourself, contact a crisis line or emergency services now.
